title: Code of Conduct
text:
The organizers of R Project Sprint 2026 are dedicated to providing a harassment-free conference experience for everyone regardless of age, gender, sexual orientation, disability, physical appearance, race, or religion (or lack thereof).
All participants at R Project Sprint 2026 are required to agree to the following code of conduct.
The code of conduct applies to all sprint activities including social events. It extends to event-specific exchanges on social media, for instance posts tagged with the identifier of the sprint (#RSprint2026) and replies to such posts.
Organizers will enforce this code throughout and expect cooperation in ensuring a safe environment for all.

title: Code of Conduct
text:
Expected Behaviour
All conference participants agree to:

Be considerate in language and actions, and respect the boundaries of fellow participants.
Refrain from demeaning, discriminatory, or harassing behaviour and language. Please refer to Unacceptable Behaviour for more details.
Alert a member of the organizing team if you notice someone in distress, or observe violations of this code of conduct, even if they seem inconsequential. Please refer to the section titled What To Do If You Witness or Are Subject To Unacceptable Behaviour for more details.

title: Code of Conduct
text:
Unacceptable Behaviour
Behaviour that is unacceptable includes, but is not limited to:

Stalking
Deliberate intimidation
Unwanted photography or recording
Sustained or willful disruption of talks or other events
Use of sexual or discriminatory imagery, comments, or jokes
Offensive comments related to age, gender, sexual orientation, disability, race or religion
Inappropriate physical contact, which can include grabbing, or massaging or hugging without consent.
Unwelcome sexual attention, which can include inappropriate questions of a sexual nature, asking for sexual favours or repeatedly asking for dates or contact information.

If you are asked to stop harassing behaviour you should stop immediately, even if your behaviour was meant to be friendly or a joke, it was clearly not taken that way and for the comfort of all conference attendees you should stop.
Attendees who behave in a manner deemed inappropriate are subject to actions listed under Procedure for Code of Conduct Violations.

title: Code of Conduct
text:
Additional Requirements for Sprint Material
Presentation slides and documents created for, or during, the sprint should not contain offensive or sexualised material.

title: Code of Conduct
section: Procedure for Code of Conduct Violations
text:
Procedure for Code of Conduct Violations
The organizing team reserves the right to determine the appropriate response for all code of conduct violations. Potential responses include:

a formal warning to stop harassing behaviour
cancellation or early termination of presentations or other contributions to the programme
expulsion from the sprint
removal/rejection of sprint contributions
removal of sponsorship acknowledgement, without return of sponsorship contribution

title: Code of Conduct
section: What To Do If You Witness or Are Subject To Unacceptable Behaviour
text:
What To Do If You Witness or Are Subject To Unacceptable Behaviour
Alert the organizing team if you notice someone in distress, or observe violations of this code of conduct, even if they seem inconsequential.
Reports should be sent via a a direct message to the moderators group on the R Project Zulip (type moderators in the “Add users” dialog box - this will expand to show everyone in the moderators group, so you can exclude individuals if necessary). You can view the current moderators if you want to check who has access to this channel.


We will take all reports by R Project Sprint 2026 participants seriously. This includes incidents outside our spaces and at any point in time. The organizing team reserve the right to exclude people from the sprint based on their past behaviour, including behaviour outside R Project Sprint 2026 spaces and behaviour towards people who are not part of the sprint.
We will respect confidentiality requests for the purpose of protecting targets of harassing behaviour. We will not name victims without their affirmative consent. Correspondence is handled confidentially and deleted after the case is resolved. All data is stored securely, access will be limited to the members of the organizing team who receive the report.
The organizing team will also provide support to victims, which may include:

providing an escort,
contacting the on-campus Security Team or off campus Emergency Services,

or otherwise assisting those experiencing harassment to ensure that they feel safe for the duration of the conference. Assistance will only be provided with affirmative consent of the victim.

title: R Project Sprint 2027
text:
Week beginning April 12, Boston, USA
Collaborate on contributions to base R!
We are pleased to announce another R Project Sprint, to be hosted in Boston, USA, in the week of Monday April 12, 2027. Novice and experienced contributors are encouraged to apply for a place, with funding available for travel and accommodation (deadline Friday 4 December). Read on for more! #RSprint2027

title: R Project Sprint 2027
text:
About the sprint
R is a popular and widely used software for data science. Like any large open source software project, it takes a lot of work to maintain and develop. Much of the work is done by a small number of volunteers and there is a need to grow the contributor community.
This sprint will bring together novice and experienced contributors, to work alongside members of the R Core Team. Participants will work collaboratively on contributions to base R and related infrastructure. The tasks will be prepared in the run-up to the event, but may include:

Reviewing, analysing and fixing bugs reported on R’s Bugzilla.
Work on new developments proposed by core developers.
Contributing to CRAN packages affected by changes in base R.
Maintaining translation infrastructure such as the Weblate instance.
Developing contributor infrastructure such as the R Development Guide.

For a short report on R Project Sprint, see the BEAR Blog post [link TBA].

title: R Project Sprint 2027
text:
Who can take part?
The sprint will involve a mixture of invited and self-nominated participants, so that we have contributors at all experience levels.
The main criteria for participation is a good knowledge of R programming and a keen interest in contributing, as we hope participants continue to contribute after the event. The table below shows the type of knowledge/skills we expect participants to have:







Skills most will have
Skills some will have




Writing R functions
Programming in C


Debugging R functions
Knowledge of S3/S4 classes and methods


Writing R help files
Expertise in statistical methods in stats, splines


Using git/Subversion
Able to build R from source



Other specialist skills would of course be welcome, e.g. expertise in Windows/macOS development, graphics and font rendering, accessibility, or compilers and build systems.
It will help if you have some experience in contributing to base R, but novice contributors will be mentored in the run-up to the event, so they are prepared.
We are also keen to foster a diverse community of contributors. If you are a member of the R-Ladies+, rainbowR, or LatinR communities, or otherwise identify as part of an underrepresented group among R contributors, then we especially encourage you to self-nominate! To ensure a welcoming environment, we have a code of conduct in place.

title: R Project Sprint 2027
text:
Apply for a place
Anyone interested to attend the sprint is encouraged to self-nominate via the application form [link TBA] by Friday 4 December. You will be asked about your experience, skills and background to help us balance participation overall.
Thanks to our sponsors, lunch and refreshments will be provided for all participants during the sprint.
Funding is also available to cover participant travel and accommodation. However if participants are able to fund their travel and accommodation from other sources this will allow more people to attend - companies or other funding bodies providing such support to participants can be acknowledged as sponsors.

title: R Project Sprint 2027
text:
Practicalities

See the US Visa Wizard for determining which visa, if any, you may need to travel to the sprint.
As travel funding is available, in-person participation is the default. However a small number of remote participants may be accommodated. There is space to make a case for remote participation on the application form.

title: R Project Sprint 2027
text:

Monday 19 April Boston Marathon, with related events over the weekend 17-18 April.
